open_points.subject: A18 startup cleanup versus K-10 file lifetime
open_points.text: A18 says value bytes no record names are kept "until the next start removes them"; K-10 says "The only files the kernel keeps beyond a run are the file fixtures of trial cases."
open_points.question: May unnamed value bytes left by a failed call remain after their run ends until the next start, or must they be removed when the run ends to preserve K-10?
options: Allow unnamed value bytes as a temporary exception to K-10 until restart
Remove such bytes when the run ends
Apply the startup rule only to failed calls not associated with a run
open_points.default_guess: Treat the new A18 text as an explicit temporary exception and remove the unnamed bytes at the next start.

open_points.subject: A18 classification of unreferenced content-addressed files
open_points.text: The data directory has "a content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures named by digest", but startup removes only "value bytes no record names" and "nothing else".
open_points.question: How does startup distinguish an unreferenced value-byte file from an unreferenced trial-fixture file, and what happens to a fixture published by a failed trial-case or capture call before its record is committed?
options: Remove every unreferenced file in the content-addressed area
Keep unreferenced fixture files and remove only value files using separate namespaces or metadata
Treat fixture bytes as value bytes for this cleanup rule
open_points.default_guess: Remove every unreferenced file in the content-addressed area, while preserving every file named by any committed record.

open_points.subject: A18 failure to remove unnamed value bytes at startup
open_points.text: "On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... are removed"; only a spool-directory removal failure is specified: "does not stop the start".
open_points.question: If an unnamed value-byte file cannot be removed, does startup fail, continue while leaving it unavailable, or handle it like an unremovable spool directory?
options: Continue, leave the file in place, and never serve it
Apply the stated non-fatal spool-directory rule to it
open_points.default_guess: Refuse to start, because the text makes only spool-directory removal failure non-fatal.
